everySettingLives: Every setting this service has lives on the page for the protocol it configures. This page is the index of that — and the form for the {mine} rows that belong to no protocol, which are facts about the process rather than about anything it speaks. It was all {total} of them until 2026-08-27; what moved is where they are DRAWN, and nothing about what they do or how they are read.
fourPlaces: A value can arrive from four places and the Source column on every one of these pages says which: a runtime override set on the page, an environment variable, the appconfig file this process was started with ({configFile}), or {defaultsFile} — the default appconfig file that one is unioned on top of. Higher beats lower, so an environment variable set on the container still wins over the file — which is what keeps every existing deployment working unchanged.
noFifthPlace: There is no fifth place. A setting with no value in either appconfig file and no environment variable stops this service from starting, by name, rather than falling back to a constant buried in a module. So every value on these pages is one somebody can find in a file — which is what makes the Source column worth reading.
fileLeftAlone: The file is left alone deliberately: a service that edited a file checked into a repository would leave a test's forgotten change behind permanently.
inMemory: Changes are in memory and are gone on restart. Nothing writes to the appconfig file, deliberately: a service that edited a file checked into a repository would leave a test's forgotten change behind permanently.
settingsHeading: {total} settings, {editable} of them changeable while this service runs
overridesInForce: {n} runtime override(s) in force, anywhere in the service:
noOverrides: No runtime overrides are in force anywhere in this service: every value is coming from the environment or from one of the two appconfig files.
resetAllHere: Reset all is here and on no protocol page, because it clears every override in the service and not only the ones below it. A button that reached that far from the Kerberos page would be the one control in this console whose blast radius was invisible from where it was pressed.
wholeTable: The whole table, group by group, in the order config.js declares them. The Page column is where that group's form is drawn; the counts are of the group, and Overridden is how many of them have a runtime override in force right now.
overJson: The whole table over JSON — every setting, whichever page edits it — is at /admin/config?format=json and GET /admin-api/config; the four actions on these pages are POST /admin-api/config/set, /set-many, /reset and /reset-all.
